newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Trial of former Coles chief starts.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Trial of former Coles chief starts.

text.p: Former Coles Myer Ltd chief executive Brian Quinn conspired in the 1980s to spend millions of dollars of the retailing giant's money on renovations to his home, a court heard on Monday.

Quinn is alleged to have been involved in a "huge fraud" on the company, conspiring to order over A$3 million of work to be done on his Melbourne mansion and pretending the expenses were for other Coles property, the prosecution told the Victorian Supreme Court.

"This is a case ... about excess in money wasting, excess as to how much work was down, excess as to the materials used, excess as to the hours spent," Prosecutor Paul Coghlan told the jury in his opening address.
"It's about overcapitalisation ... to such a degree that money spent on the house can never conceivably be recovered.
"But most of all it's a case about greed. It's a case about having your employer paying for your excesses," he said.

Quinn has pleaded not guilty to defrauding Coles Myer and the former G.J. Coles and Coy Ltd between September 1, 1982 and October 6, 1988 by falsely representing that building and renovations expenditure incurred at his Melbourne home was payable by the company.
Among the works done at the home was a full size tennis court, and tennis pavillion, a pergola and spa, extensions to the garage and home, and substantial landscaping and renovations, Coghlan said.
Inside, thousands of dollars of work was also done, including in one room which was said to have been painted at least 10 times, he said.
The defence counsel have yet to make their opening address.

Quinn was chief general manager of G.J. Coles in 1980, then managing director in 1983 before becoming chief executive of the newly-merged Coles Myer group in February 1986. He resigned from Coles Myer in 1991.
